atoms.text: This guide configures access for FrameForge, a transcoding service that reads mezzanine video files from the masters/ prefix and writes HLS renditions to the renditions/ prefix. The bucket media-masters-prod and the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role both belong to account 111122223333. Because the role and the bucket are in the same account, the grant is made entirely in the role's identity-based policy. Attach a policy to the role that allows GetObject on media-masters-prod/masters/*, PutObject on media-masters-prod/renditions/*, and ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of masters/. Do not change the bucket policy, because no statement naming the role is required and the existing policy stays as it is. Set the role's trust policy so that the FrameForge service principal can assume the role. Submit a test job that points at masters/sample.mov and confirm that .ts segments and a .m3u8 playlist appear under renditions/. If the job fails with an access denied error, check the resource ARNs in the role's policy for typos and confirm that no permissions boundary applies.

This guide configures access for FrameForge, a transcoding service that reads mezzanine video files from the masters/ prefix and writes HLS renditions to the renditions/ prefix. The bucket media-masters-prod is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role frameforge-transcode-role belongs to account 111122223333. Because requests from the role cross an account boundary, the bucket owner must grant access in the bucket policy. In account 444455556666, add a bucket policy statement that names the role ARN in account 111122223333 as the principal and allows GetObject on masters/*, PutObject on renditions/*, and ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of masters/. In account 111122223333, attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows the same actions on the same resources, since both sides must permit the request. Set the role's trust policy so that the FrameForge service principal can assume the role. Submit a test job that points at masters/sample.mov and confirm that .ts segments and a .m3u8 playlist appear under renditions/. If the job fails with an access denied error, check that the principal ARN in the bucket policy matches the role ARN exactly.

This guide grants the DocLens OCR service access to a document bucket. The service reads scanned PDF and TIFF files from the inbox/ prefix and writes extracted text as JSON files to the ocr-output/ prefix. The bucket scans-archive-eu and the IAM role doclens-ocr-role are both in account 111122223333. Since both resources share an account, the permissions are defined only in the role's identity-based policy. Create a policy with GetObject on scans-archive-eu/inbox/*, PutObject on scans-archive-eu/ocr-output/*, and ListBucket on the bucket restricted to the inbox/ prefix, then attach it to the role. The bucket policy is left unchanged, and the bucket's existing public access block settings remain in force. Configure DocLens with the role ARN and set the input and output locations to the two prefixes. Upload a two-page test PDF to inbox/ and verify that a matching .json file with per-page text blocks appears in ocr-output/. Review the role's policy first if the service reports AccessDenied on either prefix.

This guide grants the DocLens OCR service access to a document bucket. The service reads scanned PDF and TIFF files from the inbox/ prefix and writes extracted text as JSON files to the ocr-output/ prefix. The bucket scans-archive-eu is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role doclens-ocr-role is in account 111122223333. Since the role is in a different account, the bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement. The statement names the account ID 111122223333 as the principal and allows GetObject on inbox/*, PutObject on ocr-output/*, and ListBucket restricted to the inbox/ prefix. The role's own identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must allow the same actions on the same resources, and the bucket's public access block settings remain in force. Configure DocLens with the role ARN and set the input and output locations to the two prefixes. Upload a two-page test PDF to inbox/ and verify that a matching .json file with per-page text blocks appears in ocr-output/. Review both the bucket policy and the role's policy first if the service reports AccessDenied on either prefix.

This guide describes how to let PixelTrim, an image resizing service, read original photos and write derived thumbnails. PixelTrim reads JPEG and PNG files from the originals/ prefix and writes 128-pixel and 512-pixel variants to the thumbs/ prefix. The bucket product-images and the IAM role pixeltrim-worker are both in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through the identity-based policy on pixeltrim-worker, and the bucket policy is not edited. The policy allows GetObject on product-images/originals/*, PutObject on product-images/thumbs/*, and ListBucket on the bucket for the originals/ prefix. Do not grant DeleteObject, because PixelTrim never removes source files or its own output. Set the role as the execution identity in the PixelTrim project settings. Upload a sample image to originals/ and confirm that two files named with the suffixes _128 and _512 are created under thumbs/. If no thumbnails appear, inspect the role policy attached to pixeltrim-worker for missing resource paths.

This guide describes how to let PixelTrim, an image resizing service, read original photos and write derived thumbnails. PixelTrim reads JPEG and PNG files from the originals/ prefix and writes 128-pixel and 512-pixel variants to the thumbs/ prefix. The bucket product-images is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role pixeltrim-worker is in account 111122223333. Because the bucket owner is a different account, access is granted by a bucket policy statement that names the ARN of pixeltrim-worker as the principal. That statement allows GetObject on originals/*, PutObject on thumbs/*, and ListBucket on the bucket for the originals/ prefix. Do not grant DeleteObject, because PixelTrim never removes source files or its own output. Attach a matching identity-based policy to the role in account 111122223333 and set the role as the execution identity in the PixelTrim project settings. Upload a sample image to originals/ and confirm that two files named with the suffixes _128 and _512 are created under thumbs/. If no thumbnails appear, inspect the bucket policy statement for a mismatched principal ARN or missing resource paths.

This guide sets up storage access for EchoScribe, a speech transcription service that reads recorded call audio and writes transcripts. EchoScribe reads WAV and FLAC files from the recordings/ prefix and writes one JSON transcript per input file to the transcripts/ prefix. The bucket call-audio-store and the IAM role echoscribe-batch-role both belong to account 111122223333. The grant lives in the role's identity-based policy alone, and no change is made to the bucket policy. In that policy, allow GetObject on call-audio-store/recordings/*, PutObject on call-audio-store/transcripts/*, and ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of recordings/. The role has no write permission on recordings/, so source audio cannot be altered by the service. Start a batch job against recordings/2024-06/ and wait for it to report completion. Confirm that each audio file has a corresponding JSON file in transcripts/ containing timestamped segments.

This guide sets up storage access for EchoScribe, a speech transcription service that reads recorded call audio and writes transcripts. EchoScribe reads WAV and FLAC files from the recordings/ prefix and writes one JSON transcript per input file to the transcripts/ prefix. The bucket call-audio-store is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role echoscribe-batch-role belongs to account 111122223333. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement with the role ARN as the principal. The statement allows GetObject on recordings/*, PutObject on transcripts/*, and ListBucket with a prefix condition of recordings/. The statement includes no write action on recordings/, so source audio cannot be altered by the service. The role's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must also allow these actions. Start a batch job against recordings/2024-06/ and wait for it to report completion. Confirm that each audio file has a corresponding JSON file in transcripts/ containing timestamped segments.

This guide covers access for PageMorph, a document conversion service that turns DOCX files into PDF. PageMorph reads source files from the drafts/ prefix and writes converted PDFs to the published/ prefix. The bucket contracts-docs and the IAM role pagemorph-convert-role are in the same account, 111122223333. Permissions are attached to the role as an identity-based policy, and the bucket policy is not modified. The policy allows GetObject on contracts-docs/drafts/*, PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on contracts-docs/published/*, and ListBucket for the drafts/ prefix. The multipart actions are included because PDFs larger than 100 MB are uploaded in parts. Register the role ARN in the PageMorph conversion profile and select drafts/ as the input path. Convert a test DOCX and check that a PDF with the same base name appears under published/. A failed multipart upload usually points to a missing AbortMultipartUpload permission in the role's policy.

This guide covers access for PageMorph, a document conversion service that turns DOCX files into PDF. PageMorph reads source files from the drafts/ prefix and writes converted PDFs to the published/ prefix. The bucket contracts-docs is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role pagemorph-convert-role is in account 111122223333. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement that names the role ARN as the principal. The statement allows GetObject on drafts/*, PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on published/*, and ListBucket for the drafts/ prefix. The multipart actions are included because PDFs larger than 100 MB are uploaded in parts. The role's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must allow the same actions. Register the role ARN in the PageMorph conversion profile and select drafts/ as the input path. Convert a test DOCX and check that a PDF with the same base name appears under published/. A failed multipart upload usually points to a missing AbortMultipartUpload permission in either policy.

This guide explains how to give MarkStamp, a watermarking service, access to the storage it needs. MarkStamp reads camera images from the raw-photos/ prefix, reads a logo file at assets/watermarks/logo.png, and writes watermarked JPEGs to the stamped/ prefix. The bucket studio-photo-lab and the IAM role markstamp-job-role are both in account 111122223333. The grant is made only in the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy remains untouched. Include GetObject on studio-photo-lab/raw-photos/* and on the single object studio-photo-lab/assets/watermarks/logo.png, plus PutObject on studio-photo-lab/stamped/*. Add ListBucket on the bucket with prefix conditions for raw-photos/ so that the service can enumerate a batch. Set the job's output quality and watermark position in the MarkStamp configuration, and reference the role ARN. Run a batch on five sample images and verify that five files with the logo in the lower-right corner exist in stamped/.

This guide explains how to give MarkStamp, a watermarking service, access to the storage it needs. MarkStamp reads camera images from the raw-photos/ prefix, reads a logo file at assets/watermarks/logo.png, and writes watermarked JPEGs to the stamped/ prefix. The bucket studio-photo-lab is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role markstamp-job-role is in account 111122223333. The bucket owner grants access in a bucket policy statement whose principal is the role ARN. The statement includes GetObject on raw-photos/* and on the single object assets/watermarks/logo.png, plus PutObject on stamped/*. It also allows ListBucket with prefix conditions for raw-photos/ so that the service can enumerate a batch. The role's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must carry the same permissions. Set the job's output quality and watermark position in the MarkStamp configuration, and reference the role ARN. Run a batch on five sample images and verify that five files with the logo in the lower-right corner exist in stamped/.

This guide sets up access for ClipScan, a video analysis service that extracts keyframes from uploaded clips. ClipScan reads video files from the uploads/ prefix, writes JPEG keyframes to the keyframes/ prefix, and uses the tmp/ prefix for scratch files that it deletes after each job. The bucket newsroom-video-intake and the IAM role clipscan-analysis-role are both in account 111122223333. Access is granted solely by the identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. The policy allows GetObject on newsroom-video-intake/uploads/*, PutObject on newsroom-video-intake/keyframes/*, PutObject, GetObject, and DeleteObject on newsroom-video-intake/tmp/*, and ListBucket on the bucket. DeleteObject is scoped to tmp/ so that source clips and keyframes cannot be removed. Configure ClipScan with a keyframe interval of two seconds and the role ARN. Process a 30-second clip and confirm that about 15 keyframes are in keyframes/ and that tmp/ is empty afterward.

This guide sets up access for ClipScan, a video analysis service that extracts keyframes from uploaded clips. ClipScan reads video files from the uploads/ prefix, writes JPEG keyframes to the keyframes/ prefix, and uses the tmp/ prefix for scratch files that it deletes after each job. The bucket newsroom-video-intake is owned by account 444455556666, and the IAM role clipscan-analysis-role is in account 111122223333. The bucket owner adds a bucket policy statement naming the role ARN as the principal. The statement allows GetObject on uploads/*, PutObject on keyframes/*, PutObject, GetObject, and DeleteObject on tmp/*, and ListBucket on the bucket. DeleteObject is scoped to tmp/ so that source clips and keyframes cannot be removed. The role's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must allow the same actions. Configure ClipScan with a keyframe interval of two seconds and the role ARN. Process a 30-second clip and confirm that about 15 keyframes are in keyframes/ and that tmp/ is empty afterward.

This guide configures MetaHarvest, a service that extracts technical metadata from archived media files and writes it as sidecar documents. MetaHarvest lists and reads objects under the archive/ prefix and writes a JSON sidecar, containing codec, duration, and resolution fields, to the metadata/ prefix for each object. The bucket broadcast-archive and the IAM role metaharvest-indexer-role belong to account 111122223333. The grant is defined only in the role's identity-based policy, so the bucket policy needs no edit. Allow ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition of archive/, GetObject on broadcast-archive/archive/*, and PutObject on broadcast-archive/metadata/*. Because the service scans millions of keys, it paginates ListBucket calls, and no extra permission is required for pagination. Set the scan schedule to nightly in the MetaHarvest console and reference the role ARN. After the first run, open a sidecar file for a known asset and check that its duration matches the source file.

The bucket owner grants access with a bucket policy statement that names account ID 111122223333 as the principal. The statement allows ListBucket with a prefix condition of archive/, GetObject on archive/*, and PutObject on metadata/*. Because the service scans millions of keys, it paginates ListBucket calls, and no extra permission is required for pagination. The role's identity-based policy in account 111122223333 must also allow these actions, since the account-level principal only delegates to identities that their own policy permits. After the first run, open a sidecar file for a known asset and check that its duration matches the source file.
